text:
Horas, in tea language, is the name of a rope reach-
ing from the middle of a yards in its ceremony or what
called the _predecessor_, and depending about two or
three feet under the yard, for the failors to tread upon
which they are holding, resting, holding the fails, op-
ing and the fluidizing fall bombs, etc. It orders, therefore, to keep the horfe more parallel to the yard, it is
usually fupdated to it at a proper distance, by certain
roppes called dirtrops, which hang about two feet under
the yard, having my eye in their lower ends through
which the horfe place.

parsed.faithful: Horse, in tea language, is the name of a rope reaching from the middle of a yard to its extremity, or what is called the yard-arm, and depending about two or three feet under the yard, for the sailors to tread upon whilst they are loofing, reefing, or furling the sails, rigging out the studding-sail booms, &c. In order, therefore, to keep the horse more parallel to the yard, it is usually fuspended to it at proper distances, by certain ropes called firrups, which hang about two feet under the yard, having an eye in their lower ends through which the horse passes.
